title: Slow breathing for racing thoughts
keywords: breathing breathe panic anxious anxiety tension ghabrahat saans stress calm
text: Slow breathing can help the body settle when thoughts are racing. Sit comfortably, breathe in through the nose for 4 counts, then breathe out slowly through the mouth for 6 counts. Repeat about 6 times. Breathing out for longer than breathing in helps the body relax. It is a small step that may help in the moment, not a cure.

title: 5-4-3-2-1 grounding
keywords: grounding panic overwhelmed anxious present moment racing thoughts
text: When you feel overwhelmed, bring attention to the present: name 5 things you can see, 4 you can touch, 3 you can hear, 2 you can smell and 1 you can taste. Go slowly. This gives a busy mind something steady to hold on to.

title: Sleep habits that help
keywords: sleep insomnia cannot sleep awake night bedtime tired neend raat
text: A steady sleep routine can help: wake up at the same time every day, keep screens away for 30 to 60 minutes before bed, avoid tea or coffee late in the day, and write worries on paper before bed. If you are awake for more than about 20 minutes, get up, do something calm in dim light and return when sleepy. If poor sleep lasts more than two weeks, talk to a doctor or counsellor.

title: One small action when motivation is low
keywords: low mood motivation nothing to do lazy depressed no energy activity walk routine
text: When mood is low, waiting to feel better before acting often makes things worse. Try one small action first: a 10-minute walk, a shower, tea with a friend, tidying one corner. Feelings often follow action, not the other way around. Choose something so small it feels almost too easy, and repeat it daily.

title: Checking harsh thoughts
keywords: negative thoughts useless failure worthless fail self criticism overthinking
text: Harsh thoughts like 'I am useless' or 'I will fail' feel like facts but are often not. Try asking: what is the evidence for this thought, what is the evidence against it, and what would I say to a friend who thought this? Then write a fairer version, for example 'I am struggling with this, and I can ask for help'.

title: When you feel lonely
keywords: lonely loneliness alone isolated akela akelapan miss home family friends
text: Loneliness is common and does not mean something is wrong with you. Small steps help: send a short message or make a short call to someone safe today, join one regular activity with other people (a walk group, a class, a prayer or hobby group), and be kind to yourself if it feels awkward at first. Connection builds slowly.

title: Exam and work pressure
keywords: exam stress pressure study deadline overwhelmed results parents expectations pareeksha
text: When the workload feels too big, shrink it. Write down only what must be done today, pick the first small step, work for 25 to 30 minutes, then take a 5-minute break. Sleep and meals matter for memory and mood, so do not cut them first. Comparing yourself with others rarely helps; compare with your own last week.

title: Tension with family
keywords: family parents conflict fight argument anger ghar papa mummy expectations
text: Family conflict can be painful because we care about these people. Pause before reacting, name what you need underneath the argument (to be heard, to have space, to feel respected), and plan one calm sentence to say. It is fine to take a break and return to the talk later.

title: Grief and loss
keywords: grief loss death died passed away mourning missing someone
text: Grief has no fixed timetable. Crying, numbness, anger and waves of sadness are all common. Rituals, remembering the person, talking about them and keeping simple routines can help. If grief feels unbearable or does not ease over many weeks, a counsellor can support you.

title: When to talk to a professional
keywords: counsellor doctor therapist professional help two weeks persistent sad worry not coping
text: Consider talking to a counsellor or doctor if low mood, constant worry or sleep trouble lasts about two weeks or more, or if it affects study, work or relationships. Asking for help is a sign of taking care of yourself, not of weakness. Many colleges have free counselling services.
